products.name: Carvenc
products.valueProposition: When automation eliminates labor costs, what becomes economically viable?
products.timeline: Live at carvenc.vercel.app | Demo → Production Roadmap
products.description:
### The Opportunity

Architectural stone ornament was constrained by labor costs for 150 years. CNC automation eliminates 90%+ of fabrication labor. Cathedral-quality elements become economically viable at any scale.

**What This Reveals**: Cost structures aren't permanent. When major cost categories disappear (labor via CNC, design via photogrammetry/AI), previously uneconomical products become viable. The shift from **$80,000 manual carving to $6,000 CNC** isn't an improvement—it's a restructuring.

### The Value

- **For Developers**: UNESCO-quality ornament at material cost
- **For Architecture**: Economics enable styles impossible since industrialization
- **For Production**: Albanian facility (€150-300/ton material, €400-700/month labor) creates sustainable margins at competitive pricing

### Demo → Production Roadmap

**Current State**: Live demo showcasing UNESCO Heritage Scans with interactive 3D visualization

**Path to Production**:
1. Albanian facility economics validated (labor + material costs documented)
2. Photogrammetry pipeline operational (heritage sites → CNC-ready models)
3. Quality verification complete (cathedral-grade output at scale)

**The Insight**: When fabrication labor drops 90%, every architectural style from the last 150 years becomes accessible. This demonstrates what happens when automation removes a dominant cost constraint.
products.significance: This demonstrates a repeating pattern: when a dominant cost disappears, entire markets restructure. Manual stone carving wasn't expensive because of materials—it was expensive because of skilled labor. CNC + photogrammetry + AI eliminate three constraints simultaneously. The result: cathedral-quality ornament at material cost. The lesson: seemingly permanent cost structures often await the right automation to collapse them.

products.name: Agora
products.valueProposition: When AI eliminates observation constraints, why rely on proxies?
products.description:
### The Constraint That Shaped Everything

Credentials, interviews, years of experience—all proxies for capability we couldn't directly measure. Humans used proxies because **direct observation doesn't scale**. You can't watch a thousand candidates code. You can't observe problem-solving across diverse scenarios.

**What AI Changes**:
- Observation was constrained by human capacity—AI removes that limit
- Proxies were compromises, not truth (credentials predict capability at r≈0.3)
- When you can observe work quality at scale, filtering by credentials reduces quality

### The Architectural Solution

Agora enforces direct observation by making proxies unavailable. Four structural constraints ensure evaluation based only on delivery:

- **Anonymity by Default**: No names, credentials, or identity markers. Only verified delivery history.
- **Escrow Protection**: Payment locked until specifications met, cryptographically enforced.
- **Public Transaction History**: Every delivery recorded—specification, submission, acceptance/rejection.
- **Specification Discipline**: Clear acceptance criteria required. AI-assisted generation makes this practical.

### From Inference to Observation

Instead of "what kind of person should do X," the platform answers "what are the requirements for X." Every transaction creates data. Patterns emerge from thousands of transactions. The platform doesn't just facilitate work—it refines our understanding of requirements.
products.significance: This demonstrates a shift enabled by AI: when observation becomes computationally cheap, systems built on expensive observation need redesigning. Credentials existed because watching work didn't scale. With AI evaluation, we can observe the work directly. The prototype demonstrates this architecture—browse projects, view specifications, explore transaction history, all without proxy data. The insight: proxies aren't just imperfect, they're harmful when better signals are available.

products.name: Hitch
products.valueProposition: When AI learns movement patterns, why force central planning?
products.description:
### The Cowpath Philosophy

In urban planning, a "cowpath" is the trail that appears when people choose efficient routes—not planned ones. **The most effective design follows organic behavior rather than controlling it.**

**What This Reveals**:
- Traditional ridesharing forces artificial friction: browsing, negotiating, rating
- Central planning ignores local knowledge and natural patterns
- Star ratings create anxiety and punish edge cases
- Systems work better when they amplify existing behavior

### The AI Observation Approach

Instead of forcing predefined systems, Hitch observes natural movement and builds intelligence around it:

**One-Toggle Interface**: Driver Mode or Rider Mode ON. No browsing. AI handles matching.

**Pattern Learning**: From your first trip, the system learns routes and timing. Zero configuration.

**Corridor Detection**: AI identifies common routes (Tiranë → Durrës) by observation, not dictation.

**Zero Friction**: No negotiating, browsing, or ratings. WhatsApp coordination uses trusted channels. Completion percentages replace punitive stars.

### Decentralized Intelligence

Transparent pricing: (fuel cost ÷ passengers) + 30% driver premium. No surge pricing. Privacy-first: location data deleted within 24 hours. Toggle OFF means zero tracking. The system works because it follows behavior, not because it controls it.
products.significance: This demonstrates a fundamental principle: decentralized systems that observe and amplify natural behavior outperform central planning. Traditional platforms ask "how should people move?" Hitch asks "how do people actually move?" The demo proves AI can learn organic patterns, detect corridors, match riders and drivers without central control. Built for Albania's transportation patterns (commute-based earning, trust-first coordination), but the principle is universal: observe, don't dictate.
